tldr: Headlines across eight of nine country-buckets announce the same political fact: Sweden's centre-left won a narrow election, Kristersson resigned, and Andersson is returning to government. Canada and the U.S. diverge by foregrounding immigration as the decisive issue — Canada framing the win as an ideological U-turn, Fox News listing migration alongside crime and economy. Al Jazeera's headline stands apart entirely, covering Israeli voters shrugging off Western sanctions rather than the Swedish result.

evidence.quote: Kristersson resigns as PM after Sweden's centre-left
Retoma Magdalena Andersson gobierno de Suecia
Sweden's left does U-turn on immigration
Swedish immigrants vote in their own interests

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline in the corpus not about the Swedish election: Al Jazeera covers Israeli voters dismissing Western sanctions, positioning Qatar's outlet as attending to a parallel 'elections under external pressure' register entirely absent from the rest of the cluster.

The only headline to characterise the centre-left victory as an ideological concession rather than a mandate: 'does U-turn on immigration' frames the win as an accommodation of right-wing concerns, not a progressive surge.

One of the Nordic outlet's two headlines explicitly enters the post-election controversy over immigrant voters, defending their equal democratic standing ('just like other voters') — the only headline in the corpus to editorially rebut Sweden Democrat accusations that immigrant votes were illegitimate.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the Swedish election is almost universally framed as a political transition — Kristersson out, Andersson back — while Canada and the U.S. uniquely foreground immigration as the defining issue, and Al Jazeera is the sole outlier covering Israeli voters and Western sanctions rather than Sweden.
